chapter: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
title: His father's visit and the trip west
summary: His father, still with Silas Green, advised going to New York; Fields's route kept leading him farther away.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: My father was still with Silas Green. He had come over from Brunswick, Georgia, because they were located in Brunswick, Georgia. That was like the winter quarters, Brunswick, Georgia. And he came over to visit me,

and he was giving me some fatherly advice, you know. And anyway, I joined the band, Ernie Fields' band. And we got to Pensacola, Florida; we played a dance in Pensacola. Our next stop was Monroe, Louisiana. [LAUGHS] Our next stop was Tulsa, Oklahoma! I'm gettin' farther and farther' away from New York, right...! [LAUGHS] So I stayed out there with them, and I began to get attached to the guys, you know, and be like a part of the band, and so you get sentimental, you know... So I ended up staying there with him.
